question: What is the Flask application factory pattern and why do you use it?
title: Flask App Factory Pattern
direct_answer: The factory pattern creates the Flask app inside a function (create_app()) instead of at module level. This allows creating multiple app instances with different configs (testing, production), avoiding circular imports, and enabling Flask extensions to be initialized without an app context. Extension initialization moves from db = SQLAlchemy(app) to db = SQLAlchemy() at module level then db.init_app(app) inside create_app().
interviewer_intent: Tests whether the candidate knows production Flask patterns vs tutorial Flask.

sections.title: App factory benefits
sections.content:
Module-level app = Flask(__name__) is the tutorial pattern — it creates one global app. Problems: you can't easily create a test app with a test database, circular imports occur when views import from app.py which imports from models.py which imports from app.py.

Factory pattern: create_app(config=None) creates and configures the app, registers blueprints, initializes extensions, and returns the app. Create as many instances as needed.

sections.title: App factory implementation
sections.content:
# extensions.py — initialize without app
from flask_sqlalchemy import SQLAlchemy
from flask_migrate import Migrate
from flask_jwt_extended import JWTManager

db = SQLAlchemy()
migrate = Migrate()
jwt = JWTManager()

# __init__.py — app factory
from flask import Flask
from .extensions import db, migrate, jwt
from .config import Config, TestingConfig

def create_app(config_class=Config):
    app = Flask(__name__)
    app.config.from_object(config_class)

    # Initialize extensions with app
    db.init_app(app)
    migrate.init_app(app, db)
    jwt.init_app(app)

    # Register blueprints
    from .users import users_bp
    from .api import api_bp
    app.register_blueprint(users_bp, url_prefix='/users')
    app.register_blueprint(api_bp, url_prefix='/api/v1')

    return app

# Testing
def test_create_user(app):
    test_app = create_app(TestingConfig)
    with test_app.test_client() as client:
        response = client.post('/users/', json={...})
        assert response.status_code == 201

seo.metaTitle: Flask App Factory Pattern — create_app, Blueprints, Extensions
seo.metaDescription: Flask application factory: create_app() pattern for multiple configs, circular import prevention, extension init_app, and blueprint registration.

speakable_v2.hook: The app factory pattern is the difference between tutorial Flask and production Flask.

beats.content: Module-level Flask app creates a singleton — you can't have a test app with a test database. Factory pattern: create_app() creates an app, configures it, and returns it. Create as many as you need.
Extensions split into two steps: db = SQLAlchemy() at module level (no app), then db.init_app(app) inside the factory. This breaks the circular import cycle.

speakable_v2.cap: Any Flask project beyond a tutorial should use the app factory. It's the pattern all Flask plugins and testing tools expect.
